_comment: AB-517 quirk register (source of truth). Rendered into quirk-register.md by tools/discovery/pas_inventory.py --write. AB-517 owns Q-01..Q-99; other tickets use Q-<ticket>-<n>. Decisions are proposals until the sign-off table in docs/modernization/README.md is completed.

quirks.title: Leap-year renewal date
quirks.description: The new expiry date is computed as `ADD 10000` to the YYYYMMDD expiry. That is correct for every date except 29 February: 2024-02-29 becomes 20250229, which is not a valid date. DB2 rejects the POLICIES UPDATE (SQLCODE -180/-181). Because of Q-07 the program still attempts the COVERAGES date update, which fails for the same reason so the coverage dates stay unchanged, and then sends the confirmation screen.
quirks.rationale: Epic AB-516 names the leap-year renewal bug as a known defect. The fix needs a product convention for 29 Feb terms (recommendation: expire on 28 Feb of the following year, the same as `LocalDate.plusYears(1)`).
quirks.parity_note: Characterization tests record today's behaviour for 29 Feb inputs (invalid date / DB2 error) and tag it as a signed-off deviation once the fix is approved. Every other date must match exactly.

evidence.contains: does not handle leap years properly

quirks.title: Open-claims count queried but never enforced
quirks.description: 3000-CHECK-RENEWAL-ELIGIBILITY counts OPEN claims in ACMEINS.CLAIMS into WS-SQLCODE and never tests the result. The comment says the business wanted to block renewal when there are more than 3 open claims (JH 2005). Today no renewal is ever blocked for open claims. The query still needs read access to the Claims-owned table.
quirks.rationale: Turning the block on changes who gets renewed, which is a business-rule change and not part of the like-for-like migration. Migrate at parity (no block). Raise enabling the >3 rule as a separate, flagged product change.
quirks.parity_note: The Java renewal must not block on open claims. A characterization case with 4+ open claims must still renew.

evidence.contains: TODO: Business wants to block renewal if >3 open claims

quirks.title: Territory table opened but never loaded, so all factors are 1.00
quirks.description: 2000-LOAD-RATING-TABLES declares, OPENs and CLOSEs TERR_CURSOR without a single FETCH, and the comment says 'production loads all rows'. WS-TERRITORY-TABLE and WS-CLASS-TABLE are never filled. Territory, class and experience factors are hard-coded `* 1.00`, and the PREMIUMS row is inserted with literal 1.0000 for TERRITORY_FACTOR, CLASS_FACTOR, EXPERIENCE_MOD and SCHEDULE_MOD.
quirks.rationale: Epic AB-516: 'table-driven factors are the only intentional change'. The fix must be staged. First reproduce 1.00 at parity, then switch to TERRITORY_FACTORS behind a flag once Actuarial approves the table contents and the premium impact report.
quirks.parity_note: Parity baseline uses factor 1.0000. The table-driven switch is a separately approved deviation with a before/after premium diff per policy.

quirks.title: Flat 15% renewal rate-increase cap (and it can never trigger)
quirks.description: 5000-APPLY-RATE-CAP caps the renewal increase at a flat 15% (`WS-RATE-INCREASE-CAP VALUE 15.00`) instead of state-specific regulatory caps. Because 4000-CALCULATE-NEW-PREMIUM always applies exactly +5% (Q-05), the 15% branch is unreachable today.
quirks.rationale: State-specific caps are a regulatory/pricing change, which the epic puts out of scope. Port the flat cap at parity as configuration (cap = 15.00) so Compliance can later supply per-state values without a code change.
quirks.parity_note: Tests cover the cap boundary in isolation (unit level), even though the end-to-end renewal can never exceed 5% today.

evidence.contains: Using flat 15% cap for now (TODO: state-specific caps)

quirks.title: Renewal premium is a hard-coded +5% uplift
quirks.description: Every renewal premium is the old TOTAL_PREMIUM * 1.05. It does not use PREMBAT, the PREMIUMS table, coverages or territory. The comment says actuarial never provided the table.
quirks.rationale: This is a rating rule. The epic says rating moves at parity. Make it a configurable uplift (default 1.05).
quirks.parity_note: Golden cases compare renewal premiums to the cent, with truncation (see Q-06).

quirks.title: Arithmetic truncates instead of rounding
quirks.description: No COMPUTE in PAS uses ROUNDED, so intermediate and final results are truncated toward zero into the receiving PIC (V99 for money, V9(06) for the pro-rata factor). Examples: PREMBAT tax = premium * 0.0350 truncated to cents, POLRNW premium * 1.05 truncated to cents.
quirks.rationale: Changing to HALF_UP would change premiums by a cent on many policies. The epic requires cent-level parity, so use BigDecimal with RoundingMode.DOWN at the same scale as each COBOL receiving field.
quirks.parity_note: The parity harness compares to the cent. Java code must use BigDecimal with explicit scale + RoundingMode.DOWN wherever COBOL COMPUTE has no ROUNDED.

quirks.title: Renewal continues after a failed policy UPDATE
quirks.description: If the POLICIES UPDATE fails, 6000-CREATE-RENEWAL-TERM sends the error text, but 0000-MAIN-LOGIC still runs 7000-UPDATE-COVERAGES (moves coverage dates to the new term) and 8000-SEND-CONFIRMATION. The terminal shows a confirmation and coverages can be moved to a term the policy never got. CICS syncpoint-on-return commits the coverage change.
quirks.rationale: Partial updates break data integrity. The target must do the whole renewal in one transaction and roll it back on any failure.
quirks.parity_note: Characterization documents the current partial-update outcome. The Java service is expected to differ (all-or-nothing), so this is a signed-off deviation.

evidence.contains: MOVE 'DB2 ERROR UPDATING RENEWAL' TO WS-ERROR-MSG

quirks.title: Generated policy number overflows PIC X(12): last digit dropped, numbers collide
quirks.description: 4000-GENERATE-POLICY-NUM STRINGs 'POL' + WS-POLICY-SEQ (PIC 9(10), zero-padded) into POLICY-NUMBER PIC X(12). That is 13 characters, so the STRING overflows and drops the last digit. POLICY_SEQ starts at 1000000, so sequence values 1000000-1000009 all become 'POL000100000', and 9 of every 10 inserts would hit a duplicate key. The format 'POL' + 9 digits also differs from the 'POL-########' numbers in the facade seed data and API snapshots.
quirks.owner: Mainframe team (mainframe-ops@acme.com) + Product Owner, Policy Administration
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: The epic requires existing policy numbers to stay exactly the same. The mainframe team must confirm the production algorithm (the load module may differ from this source) before the Java generator is written. Existing numbers are preserved. Generation of new numbers must not collide.
quirks.parity_note: Parity tests must assert the production format confirmed by the mainframe team, not this source. Blocked on FU-05.

quirks.title: New-policy dates never moved to the DB2 host variables
quirks.description: 5000-INSERT-POLICY copies number, type, holder, agent, branch, amounts and flags into DCLPOLICIES. It never sets POL-EFF-DT, POL-EXP-DT or POL-INCEPT-DT, but the INSERT binds them to the NOT NULL EFFECTIVE_DATE/EXPIRY_DATE columns and to INCEPTION_DATE. 6100-WRITE-COVERAGE binds the same uninitialised fields. As written, the insert would fail or store garbage dates. No rule for the new expiry date (effective + 1 year?) exists anywhere in the repo.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: Either the production source differs, or PNEW cannot create policies. The target must set effective, expiry and inception explicitly. The expiry rule needs product confirmation.
quirks.parity_note: Blocked on FU-05. Capture real PNEW outputs from production or the test region before writing the new-business parity tests.

quirks.title: Default coverages hard-coded per policy type with unset amounts
quirks.description: 6000-INSERT-COVERAGES writes fixed coverage codes per type: AUT gets AUTL+AUTP, HOM gets PROP+LIAB, COM gets PROP+LIAB+WKCP. LIF and HLT get no coverages. COV-LIMIT, COV-DEDUCTIBLE and COV-PREMIUM are never set, and COV-SEQUENCE-NUM is incremented without being initialised, so the stored amounts and sequence numbers depend on leftover storage.
quirks.rationale: Keep the per-type default coverage codes (behaviour consumers see). Fix the uninitialised amounts and sequence (explicit 0 / start at 1). Product must confirm whether LIF/HLT really get no coverages.
quirks.parity_note: Tests assert the codes and descriptions per type. Amounts are asserted as 0.00 and sequence numbers as 1..n (signed-off deviation if production differs).

evidence.contains: TODO: This should be table-driven but never got refactored

quirks.title: Only the last validation error is reported
quirks.description: Each failed check in 3000-VALIDATE-INPUT overwrites WS-ERROR-MSG, so only the last failure is shown. The DB2 policyholder lookup runs even after earlier checks failed (and after a failed RECEIVE). Precedence, last wins: holder not found > limit zero > effective date in past > type required > holder id required.
quirks.rationale: 3270 users and scripts may depend on which message appears. Keep the same precedence on the CICS-equivalent path. A new REST API may additionally return every violation.
quirks.parity_note: Golden cases with several invalid fields assert the single message selected by the precedence above.

evidence.contains: MOVE 'POLICYHOLDER ID IS REQUIRED' TO WS-ERROR-MSG

quirks.title: New-business premium is taken from screen input, not rated
quirks.description: POLICIES.TOTAL_PREMIUM on a new policy is whatever the operator keyed into the map. No rating happens at quote/bind. PREMBAT later writes rated rows to PREMIUMS but never updates POLICIES.TOTAL_PREMIUM (see Q-26).
quirks.rationale: Introducing rating at bind is a product change and out of scope.
quirks.parity_note: The new-business API accepts the premium as input. Tests assert it is stored unchanged.

quirks.title: TD queue names longer than 4 characters: request and decision share one queue
quirks.description: POLNEW writes the underwriting request and UNDWRT writes the decision with EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD, using 48-byte names 'ACME.PAS.UNDERWRITING.REQUEST' / '...DECISION'. A CICS TD queue id is 4 characters, so both resolve to the same queue 'ACME'. The routing to IBM MQ, FileNet and the underwriting work queue lives in CSD/DCT and MQ definitions that are not in this repo. POLNEW ignores a failed write (policy committed, no UW request sent), and UNDWRT never checks RESP.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: The target publishes two distinct, durable events (underwriting.requested, underwriting.decided) with at-least-once delivery. The mainframe team must supply the real queue/route definitions and the consumers (FileNet, UW queue) must confirm the payload (raw POLICY-RECORD bytes, 125 bytes).
quirks.parity_note: The new events are JSON (pas-events PasEvent), so there is no byte payload to compare. AB-525 compares the decision fields of the POLICY-RECORD (policy number, UW status, risk score) field by field (UndwrtDecisionAdapter); a byte-for-byte POLICY-RECORD check returns only if consumers keep the 125-byte payload through the AB-528 MQ bridge (FU-525-7).

quirks.title: Risk score sign loss and truncation
quirks.description: WS-RISK-SCORE is unsigned PIC 9(04). A preferred-tier customer with a high credit score goes negative after `SUBTRACT 100` and is stored as the absolute value (credit 850: 25 - 100 = -75, stored as 75). The score is then MOVEd to POLICY-RISK-SCORE PIC 9(03), which drops the thousands digit for scores of 1000 or more (possible: up to ~1850). The MQ message and the result map show e.g. 250 while UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS/POLICIES get 1250.
quirks.rationale: Accept/refer/decline uses the full WS value, so the decision itself is not affected by the truncation. The fix: clamp at 0, never truncate, and send the full score in the event. Underwriting must confirm the clamp (sign loss can move a score a few points).
quirks.parity_note: Characterization covers credit 850+/preferred and scores of 1000+. Java differs only in the message/display score and in negative clamping. Record both as signed-off deviations. The clamp is not only cosmetic: when the absolute value pushed the COBOL score over a band boundary, Java decides differently (credit 850 preferred, 4 claims, limit over 5,000,000: COBOL 325 RS, Java 250 AP). Fixture preferred-high-credit-band-crossing and known difference KD-11 cover it; Underwriting must sign off the band change.

quirks.title: Loss ratio overflows at 1000%, so extreme losers can escape the surcharge
quirks.description: WS-LOSS-RATIO is PIC S9(03)V99. A loss ratio of 1000% or more loses its high-order digit (1050.00 becomes 050.00), so the `> 80` test fails and the +200 surcharge is not applied to the very worst risks. The query reads INCURRED_AMOUNT from ACMEINS.CLAIMS over 5 years.
quirks.rationale: This is a clear defect against the documented intent and only affects extreme loss histories. Underwriting must confirm.
quirks.parity_note: A characterization case with incurred = 11x premium records the current (no surcharge) result as a signed-off deviation.

quirks.title: Accumulation-limit reason is overwritten
quirks.description: 4000-CHECK-ACCUMULATION adds 300 and writes 'ACCUMULATION LIMIT EXCEEDED FOR BRANCH ...' into WS-DECISION-REASON. 5000-RENDER-DECISION then always overwrites the reason with the band text, so the audit trail never says why. The branch sum includes the policy being underwritten (if active), and the $500M limit is hard-coded.
quirks.rationale: Keep the score effect (+300 over $500M per branch, made configurable) and record the accumulation reason alongside the band text.
quirks.parity_note: Score and decision code must match. DECISION_REASON text differs (signed-off deviation).

quirks.title: Decision codes RS/RM are outside the POLICY-RECORD UW status domain
quirks.description: UNDWRT writes AP / RS / RM / DC to POLICIES.UW_STATUS and UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS.DECISION_CODE. The POLICY-RECORD copybook only defines AP / PN / DC / RF, so consumers decoding by copybook (FileNet, extracts, Broker Portal) see undefined values for referrals.
quirks.rationale: The stored codes are the DB contract read by the extracts and the facade. Keep RS/RM and document the full domain {AP, PN, DC, RF, RS, RM}.
quirks.parity_note: Target enums must accept and emit all six codes unchanged.

quirks.title: Second underwriting decision on the same day is silently lost
quirks.description: UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS has PRIMARY KEY (POLICY_NUMBER, DECISION_DATE). A second PUWR run for the same policy on the same day fails with -803. SQLCODE is not checked, so POLICIES is still updated and the message is still sent, but the audit row is missing.
quirks.rationale: The audit trail must be complete. The target keys decisions by timestamp/sequence. The data migration keeps the existing rows.
quirks.parity_note: Deviation: Java records every decision. Reconciliation compares the latest decision per policy per day.

quirks.title: Endorsement type never populated from the screen
quirks.description: The map is RECEIVEd INTO POLICY-RECORD, but WS-ENDORSEMENT-TYPE is a separate working-storage field with no VALUE and is never moved. The 'ENDORSEMENT TYPE IS REQUIRED' check and the ENDORSEMENT_TYPE inserted into ENDORSEMENTS therefore depend on uninitialised storage. The DB2 read also runs after a failed RECEIVE.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: The production source or the BMS map (not in repo) may populate it differently. The target takes the endorsement type as required input.
quirks.parity_note: Blocked on FU-05 / FU-07: capture real PEND inputs and outputs.

quirks.title: Pro-rata factor computed but never applied
quirks.description: 4000-CALCULATE-PRORATA computes days remaining / days in term, but nothing uses WS-PRORATA-FACTOR and WS-PREMIUM-ADJUST is never computed. The ENDORSEMENTS row stores an uninitialised adjustment and TOTAL_PREMIUM is incremented by it (expected 0). Days fields are unsigned PIC 9(03), so endorsing after expiry gives a positive 'remaining', and terms over 999 days truncate.
quirks.owner: Product Owner, Policy Administration + Actuarial / Pricing lead
quirks.rationale: The header promises a pro-rata premium adjustment. Fixing it changes premiums, so Product/Actuarial must define the rule (pro-rata of what amount?). Until then the target stores 0.00 explicitly.
quirks.parity_note: Parity: PREMIUM_ADJUSTMENT = 0.00 and TOTAL_PREMIUM unchanged. Enabling pro-rata is a separately approved change.

quirks.title: Endorsement types have no type-specific processing; CAN does not cancel
quirks.description: CAD/CRM/LCH/ACH/CAN are declared, but every type does the same thing: insert an ENDORSEMENTS row and rewrite TOTAL_PREMIUM. No coverage is added or removed, no limit or address changes, and a cancellation ('CAN', mid-term cancellation added 2007) does not set POLICY_STATUS to CN. The endorsement EFFECTIVE_DATE is always today (no back/forward dating). DESCRIPTION is never written.
quirks.rationale: The migration ports what the program actually does. Real endorsement processing (and cancellation) is a new capability that needs its own spec, so raise it as a follow-up rather than silently adding it.
quirks.parity_note: The Java endorsement path must not change coverages or status for any type at parity.

quirks.title: Endorsement continues after a failed INSERT
quirks.description: If the ENDORSEMENTS insert fails, the error text is set, but 5000 still updates POLICIES.TOTAL_PREMIUM, and 6000 (audit) and 7000 (confirmation screen) still run, because 0000-MAIN-LOGIC only checks errors before 4000.
quirks.rationale: Same as Q-07: the target must be all-or-nothing.
quirks.parity_note: Signed-off deviation: Java rolls back.

quirks.title: Regulatory endorsement audit trail lives in a CICS TS queue
quirks.description: The 2016 'regulatory' audit writes POLICY-RECORD to TS queue 'ENDORSEMENT-AUDIT'. That name is longer than the 8-character (16 with QNAME) TS limit, a TS queue is not a durable audit store, and nothing in the repo reads or archives it. The record does not contain the endorsement type or amount.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: Compliance must say what the audit must hold and how long. The target writes a durable, append-only audit record (plus event). The mainframe team must confirm who drains the TSQ today.
quirks.parity_note: Not part of parity. Audit content is defined by Compliance (FU-09).

quirks.title: Inquiry reads customer and coverages but displays only the policy header
quirks.description: POLQRY reads POLICY_HOLDERS (SQLCODE unchecked) and up to 20 coverages into WS-COVERAGE-TABLE, but SENDs only POLICY-RECORD to map POLQDET. The header claims 'coverage detail display' and an 'API flag check for facade' (2022), but no API_FLAG check exists. The REST facade does not filter on API_FLAG either.
quirks.owner: Product Owner, Policy Administration + Java facade owner (t.nguyen@acme.com)
quirks.rationale: The new inquiry API keeps the facade contract (compat snapshots). API_FLAG stays informational (no filtering). Product must confirm whether API_FLAG='N' policies should really be visible to API consumers. AB-524: GET /api/v1/policies/{policyNumber} returns API_FLAG='N' policies as before; the holder POLQRY reads is exposed additively at /policyholder (masked unless pas.policyholder.read).
quirks.parity_note: The inquiry API must match compat/api/snapshots byte-for-byte, including returning policies with API_FLAG='N'.

evidence.contains: Added API flag check for facade

quirks.title: Premium batch stops at the first INSERT error
quirks.description: 3000-PROCESS-POLICIES loops `PERFORM 3100-FETCH-POLICY UNTIL SQLCODE NOT = 0`, but 3100 runs the PREMIUMS INSERT after the FETCH. A failed INSERT leaves SQLCODE non-zero and ends the loop, so all remaining policies are skipped and the job ends RC=4 with partial output.
quirks.rationale: The epic requires the full book in under 30 min with safe reruns. The target processes every policy, records per-policy errors and continues.
quirks.parity_note: Signed-off deviation for runs that hit an insert error. Otherwise per-policy outputs must match.

quirks.title: Premium batch is not rerunnable: daily duplicate PREMIUMS key
quirks.description: Every daily run INSERTs (POLICY_NUMBER, COVERAGE_SEQ=1, TERM_EFFECTIVE_DATE) for each active policy. PREMIUMS has that as its primary key, so from the second run in a term every insert hits -803. Combined with Q-25, a rerun stops at the first policy: its INSERT gets -803, the loop ends, no PREMIUMS rows are written for any policy, and the job ends RC=4 (the report holds one detail line plus the summary). Only one row per policy (COVERAGE_SEQ 1) is written, and POLICIES.TOTAL_PREMIUM is never updated.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: The epic requires safe reruns. Recommend an idempotent upsert per (policy, coverage seq, term). The mainframe team must explain how production avoids the duplicate (pre-delete step, different source?).
quirks.parity_note: Parity compares the resulting PREMIUMS rows for a single run on a clean term. Reruns must be no-ops in Java.

quirks.title: Premium formula: base by policy type only, flat 3.5% tax, flat $25 surcharge
quirks.description: Base premium depends only on POLICY_TYPE (AUT 850, HOM 1200, COM 5000, LIF 400, HLT 3500, anything else 1000; e.g. 'CGL' in the facade data gets 1000). Coverages, limits and deductibles are ignored. Tax is a flat 3.5% (TODO state-specific), the surcharge a flat $25, and the installment code is always 'AN'.
quirks.rationale: Rating moves at parity. Only the factor tables change intentionally (Q-03). Move the constants to configuration with the same values.
quirks.parity_note: Golden PREMIUMS rows per policy type, including an unknown type, compared to the cent.

quirks.title: Premium batch return codes and notifications are inverted
quirks.description: If the report file fails to open, PREMBAT sets WS-RETURN-CODE to 16 and does STOP RUN without moving it to RETURN-CODE, so the job ends RC=0. In the JCL, STEP030 has COND=(4,LT,STEP010), which bypasses it when RC > 4. It therefore sends 'PREMIUM BATCH COMPLETED WITH WARNINGS' on clean runs (RC 0) and on warnings (RC 4), and stays silent on real failures. STEP020 (IEFBR14) does nothing.
quirks.rationale: Operations alerting must reflect reality. The target emits success/warning/failure status and metrics.
quirks.parity_note: Not part of data parity. Covered by the scheduler/alerting runbook.

quirks.title: Premium report STRINGs a packed-decimal field
quirks.description: The report line STRINGs WS-FINAL-PREMIUM (COMP-3) and DISPLAY counters into a 132-byte line. STRING only accepts DISPLAY items, so either the production source differs or the report holds raw packed bytes. The report layout (ACME.PAS.REPORTS.PREMIUM, LRECL 132) cannot be pinned down from the repo.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: Preserve whatever production actually produces. The mainframe team must provide a sample report.
quirks.parity_note: Byte-level report comparison waits for a production sample (FU-13).

quirks.title: Extract jobs run DSNTEP2, which does not write the output DDs
quirks.description: STEP010/STEP020 of DAILY-EXTRACT and STEP010 of MONTHLY-EXPOSURE run DSNTEP2 with in-stream SELECTs. DSNTEP2 writes formatted, paginated output to SYSPRINT. It does not write to POLOUT/COVOUT/EXPOUT, so as written the transferred datasets would be empty. The byte layout of the Claims feed (LRECL 200/150) and the actuarial 'CSV' (LRECL 300) is not defined anywhere in the repo.
quirks.owner: Mainframe team (mainframe-ops@acme.com) + Claims team (owner of ACMEINS.CLAIMS and the Claims import) + Actuarial / Pricing lead
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: Downstream consumers parse fixed-width layouts (epic risk). Capture real production files and the actual unload utility (DSNTIAUL / custom program?) and preserve them byte-for-byte.
quirks.parity_note: Byte-level file comparison against captured production files. Blocked on FU-13.

quirks.title: Claims extract mixes a policy delta with a full coverage dump
quirks.description: The policy extract selects AC/PN policies with LAST_UPDATED >= CURRENT DATE - 1 DAY (a delta with a ~1-day window that depends on run time). The coverage extract dumps every active coverage (full). The header also promises a CUSTOMER extract and a Broker Portal refresh, but no step produces them. Status codes EX/LP/CN never reach Claims.
quirks.owner: Claims team (owner of ACMEINS.CLAIMS and the Claims import)
quirks.rationale: The Claims VB6 import was built against this exact mix. Changing delta/full semantics needs Claims sign-off.
quirks.parity_note: Run the extract on a fixed clock and compare with the captured production file. The delta window boundaries are part of the contract.

quirks.title: Plaintext FTP of PII feeds despite a documented 'encryption step'
quirks.description: Both feeds are sent with the z/OS FTP client program (user ACMEFTP) in clear text. The DAILY-EXTRACT header says 'Added encryption step (regulatory)' in 2012, but no such step exists.
quirks.rationale: Epic success criterion: 'No unencrypted file transfers'. Replace with SFTP/managed transfer. Consumers must confirm the new endpoint.
quirks.parity_note: File content stays byte-identical. Only the transport changes.

quirks.title: Extract datasets are not rerunnable (fixed DSN, DISP=NEW)
quirks.description: POLOUT and COVOUT use fixed names (no date qualifier or GDG) with DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE). The second night fails with 'duplicate data set name' unless something outside this job deletes them. The dated DSNs in PREMIUM-BATCH/MONTHLY-EXPOSURE fail on a same-day rerun for the same reason.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: Target outputs must be idempotent per business date. Operations must confirm the current cleanup job.
quirks.parity_note: Not part of data parity.

quirks.title: Exposure 'POLICY_COUNT' counts coverages; documented cat/cyber fields absent
quirks.description: POLICY_COUNT is COUNT(*) over the POLICIES x COVERAGES join, grouped by coverage attributes, so it counts coverage rows, not policies. The header mentions catastrophe-zone (2008) and cyber (2015) fields that are not in the query. ORDER BY only covers the first two grouping columns, so row order inside a group is not deterministic.
quirks.rationale: Actuarial SAS models are calibrated on this output. Keep the semantics and pin the row order (full ORDER BY) only if Actuarial agrees.
quirks.parity_note: Compare as an order-insensitive multiset within (POLICY_TYPE, BRANCH_CODE) unless Actuarial confirms the order.

quirks.title: Data values outside the COBOL code domains
quirks.description: The facade seed data and the API contract snapshots contain values no COBOL 88-level knows: policy number format 'POL-########', POLICY_TYPE 'CGL', coverage codes DWEL/PERS/COLL/PREM/PROD, RISK_TIER 'A'/'B'. The copybooks define AUT/HOM/COM/LIF/HLT, PROP/LIAB/AUTP/AUTL/WKCP/UMBR/CYBR/TERR and P/S/U. Programs treat unknown values as 'other' (e.g. PREMBAT base 1000, UNDWRT no tier adjustment).
quirks.rationale: Production data may contain the same drift. The target must accept the full observed domain (string codes, not closed enums) until data profiling (FU-16) proves otherwise.
quirks.parity_note: Parity fixtures include out-of-domain codes.

quirks.title: Facade: no authentication, open actuator, default DB2 password
quirks.description: The Spring Boot 1.5 facade has no authentication (comment: relies on VPN), turns off actuator management security in the production application.properties, exposes Swagger UI, and defaults DB2_PASSWORD to 'changeme' in application.properties and the Dockerfile.
quirks.rationale: Epic success criterion: all reads and writes through authenticated, authorised APIs. Delivered by the inquiry/auth tickets, and the compat gate approves the 401/403 change explicitly. AB-524: pas-policy-service validates OAuth 2.0 JWTs on every request, enforces pas.policy.read plus agent/branch/book entitlement, and needs pas.ops.read for info/metrics; the facade is retired through the gated plan in docs/pas/facade-retirement.md.
quirks.parity_note: API contract snapshots stay the same apart from the approved auth change.

quirks.title: Facade serialises dates as strings but LAST_UPDATED as epoch milliseconds
quirks.description: The facade maps DATE columns with ResultSet.getDate (serialised by Jackson as yyyy-MM-dd) and LAST_UPDATED with getTimestamp (serialised as epoch milliseconds in the JVM default time zone). RENEWAL_COUNT, RISK_SCORE and COINSURANCE_PCT are Java primitives, so NULL becomes 0. Not-found answers 404 with an empty body.
quirks.rationale: Existing consumers parse these shapes (compat/api/snapshots/policies-v1.json). The inquiry API keeps them; the time zone is configurable (PAS_INQUIRY_TIMESTAMP_ZONE) until FU-524-2 confirms the production value.
quirks.parity_note: FacadeContractIT runs compat/api/check_api.py against pas-policy-service; lastUpdated is type-checked only.

quirks.title: Local H2 schema has a policy -> holder FK that DB2 lacks
quirks.description: java-facade/src/main/resources/schema.sql declares FK_POL_HOLDER (POLICIES.POLICYHOLDER_ID -> POLICY_HOLDERS.CUST_ID). The DB2 DDL has no such constraint, so production can hold policies whose holder does not exist. POLNEW checks the holder only at create time.
quirks.rationale: Keep DB2 semantics (no FK) during dual-run so that migration never rejects production rows. Add the FK only after profiling shows zero orphans.
quirks.parity_note: Data migration reconciliation reports orphan counts.

quirks.title: Premium batch is one unit of work for the whole book
quirks.description: PREMBAT never COMMITs. The whole ~4-hour run is one DB2 unit of work, committed only when the DSN RUN ends normally. An abend rolls back every row and holds locks on PREMIUMS for hours. Processing is single-threaded, ordered by POLICY_NUMBER.
quirks.rationale: Epic success criterion: under 30 minutes with safe reruns. The target commits in chunks, is restartable and runs in parallel.
quirks.parity_note: Final PREMIUMS state must match for a completed run, whatever the chunking.

quirks.title: Renewal resets UW status to pending but never requests underwriting
quirks.description: 6000-CREATE-RENEWAL-TERM sets POLICY_STATUS 'AC' and UW_STATUS 'PN' but sends no underwriting request (unlike POLNEW), so renewed policies stay UW 'PN' until someone runs PUWR by hand. The new term always starts at the old expiry, whenever the renewal is run. Expired (EX) policies of any age are eligible. The 2020 COVID grace flag WS-COVID-GRACE is declared but never used.
quirks.owner: Underwriting lead + Product Owner, Policy Administration
quirks.rationale: Changing the renewal underwriting workflow is a business change. Port as-is, and raise the missing UW referral and the lapse limit as a follow-up.
quirks.parity_note: Java renewal sets UW_STATUS 'PN' and emits no underwriting request.

quirks.title: Nothing in the repo moves a new policy from PN to AC
quirks.description: POLNEW inserts POLICY_STATUS 'PN'. UNDWRT updates only UW_STATUS and RISK_SCORE, never POLICY_STATUS. Every downstream reader filters on status: PREMBAT, accumulation and the exposure feed read only 'AC', and the Claims extract reads AC/PN. So the PN -> AC activation step must live outside this repo (another program, manual SQL, or the BMS flow).
quirks.owner: Mainframe team (mainframe-ops@acme.com) + Product Owner, Policy Administration
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: The activation path must be found before new business is migrated. Until then the target leaves status changes to an explicit activation call.
quirks.parity_note: Blocked on FU-05.

quirks.title: Zero-premium renewal divides by zero (no guard, no ON SIZE ERROR)
quirks.description: 4000-CALCULATE-NEW-PREMIUM computes WS-RATE-CHANGE-PCT as (new - old) / WS-OLD-PREMIUM * 100 with no zero check and no ON SIZE ERROR. A policy whose TOTAL_PREMIUM is 0 (POLNEW never rates new business, Q-12) therefore divides by zero. UNDWRT guards the same kind of division with `IF POLICY-TOTAL-PREMIUM > 0`. On z/OS a packed-decimal divide by zero most likely raises a decimal-divide exception (S0CB), so the PRWL task abends ASRA and CICS backs out the unit of work; the exact outcome depends on compiler options and must be verified by the mainframe team.
quirks.owner: Product Owner, Policy Administration + Mainframe team (mainframe-ops@acme.com)
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: An abend is not a business behaviour worth preserving. The Java renewal must define the zero-premium case explicitly. Recommendation: treat the rate change as 0% (new premium stays 0, so the cap cannot apply) and renew normally, unless the Product Owner prefers to reject the renewal with a clear message.
quirks.parity_note: Characterization records the legacy outcome for a zero-premium renewal (expected abend / no update) as a signed-off deviation. Every non-zero premium must match exactly.

quirks.title: Audit user columns hold only 8 characters
quirks.component: POLICIES, ENDORSEMENTS, UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS, PREMIUMS; POLICY-RECORD, PREMIUM-RECORD
quirks.description: Every 'who changed this' column is CHAR(8): POLICIES.UPDATED_BY, ENDORSEMENTS.PROCESSED_BY, UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS.UNDERWRITER_ID and OVERRIDE_BY, PREMIUMS.CALC_BY, and the copybook fields POLICY-UPDATED-BY / PREM-CALC-BY are PIC X(08). No person is recorded today. Most writes store the program name: POLICIES.UPDATED_BY = 'POLNEW', 'POLRNW', 'POLEND' or 'UNDWRT'; ENDORSEMENTS.PROCESSED_BY = 'POLEND'; PREMIUMS.CALC_BY = 'PREMBAT'. UNDWRT writes the literal 'SYSTEM' to UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS.UNDERWRITER_ID, OVERRIDE_BY is never set by the COBOL (NULL), and POLICIES.UPDATED_BY defaults to 'SYSTEM' for any insert that omits it (POLNEW sets it explicitly). An OIDC principal (subject or e-mail) from the new APIs does not fit, and widening the columns would change the 125-byte POLICY-RECORD sent to MQ consumers and the facade contract.
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending ARB and Security sign-off (ADR 0001 D5)
quirks.rationale: Column widths and copybook layouts are guarded contracts (compat gate) and stay unchanged while DB2 is the system of record. The Java service writes an 8-character service id (or a mapped 8-character user id) into these columns, and records the full authenticated principal in the new append-only audit table (ADR 0001, component DS-05).
quirks.parity_note: Parity baselines compare the 8-character columns as written today: the program names above, 'SYSTEM' in UNDERWRITER_ID (and in UPDATED_BY wherever a row was inserted without it), and NULL in OVERRIDE_BY. Values written by the new APIs are an approved difference once the id mapping is signed off.

quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending DBA and Data governance sign-off
quirks.title: Copybook last-updated fields hold a date, the columns a timestamp
quirks.description: POLICY-LAST-UPDATED and CUST-LAST-UPDATED are PIC 9(08) (YYYYMMDD), while POLICIES.LAST_UPDATED and POLICY_HOLDERS.LAST_UPDATED are TIMESTAMP. Any record built from a row loses the time of day, and a row built from a record gets midnight.
quirks.rationale: The copybook layout is a frozen contract for downstream consumers. The Java codecs write only the date part and read the date as midnight; the database keeps full timestamps.
quirks.parity_note: Parity compares these copybook fields as dates only; table comparisons use the full timestamp.

quirks.component: POLICIES.RENEWAL_COUNT, POLICIES.RISK_SCORE, COVERAGES.COINSURANCE_PCT, POLICY_HOLDERS.CREDIT_SCORE; POLICY-RECORD, COVERAGE-RECORD, CUSTOMER-RECORD
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending DBA and Data governance sign-off
quirks.title: Nullable numeric columns have no null in the copybooks
quirks.description: RENEWAL_COUNT, RISK_SCORE, COINSURANCE_PCT and CREDIT_SCORE are nullable SMALLINT columns, but their copybook fields are unsigned PIC 9(03), which has no null and no sign. A null is written as 000 and reads back as 0; a negative value or one above 999 cannot be written.
quirks.rationale: The copybook layout is frozen. The codecs write null as zeros and reject values the picture cannot hold instead of truncating them, so no data is silently changed.
quirks.parity_note: Parity treats null and 0 as equal for these copybook fields.

quirks.title: Failed map RECEIVE falls through the whole program
quirks.description: When EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP fails, 2000-READ-POLICY-DATA (UNDWRT) and 2000-READ-EXISTING-POLICY (POLRNW) set the error text and GO TO 2000-EXIT. The paragraph is PERFORMed without THRU, so GO TO leaves the PERFORM range: control continues at 2000-EXIT and falls through every following paragraph in source order instead of returning to 0000-MAIN-LOGIC. UNDWRT therefore scores an empty record (base 400), writes an UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS row and updates POLICIES for the received key, sends the TD message and result map, and only then sends the error text. POLRNW reaches 4000-CALCULATE-NEW-PREMIUM with a zero premium and divides by zero (as in Q-41). Found by the AB-520 characterization harness.
quirks.owner: Mainframe team (mainframe-ops@acme.com) + Product Owner, Policy Administration
quirks.decision_status: proposed - pending mainframe-team verification against production load module
quirks.rationale: Writing a decision or renewing after a failed screen receive is never intended. The Java APIs validate the request and reject it before any read or write. The legacy behaviour is recorded so the difference is explicit.
quirks.parity_note: Golden cases undwrt-decision/map-receive-failure and polrnw-renewal/map-receive-failure record today's fall-through. The Java versions return an error with no writes, recorded as known differences once this decision is signed off.

quirks.title: PREMBAT premium arithmetic has no ON SIZE ERROR: overflow silently drops high-order digits
quirks.description: No COMPUTE in 3200-CALCULATE-PREMIUM has ON SIZE ERROR. A result wider than its receiving field (WS-TERR/CLASS/MOD/FINAL-PREMIUM S9(09)V99, WS-TAX-AMOUNT S9(07)V99) keeps only the low-order digits, so a premium of 1,000,000,000.00 would be stored as 0.00. With today's hardcoded rates and 1.00 factors no input can reach the limit; table-driven factors (Q-03) or loaded base rates could.
quirks.rationale: Silently truncated premiums are never correct. The Java rating component (pas-rating PremiumCalculator) checks every step against the COBOL field width and throws RatingOverflowException instead; the batch job reports the policy as an error.
quirks.parity_note: Unreachable with the current rates, so no golden file differs. PremiumCalculatorBoundaryTest covers the largest value that fits and the first that overflows for each field.

quirks.title: Daily extract window depends on when the job starts
quirks.description: The policy delta selects LAST_UPDATED >= CURRENT DATE - 1 DAY, evaluated when DSNTEP2 runs. A run delayed or restarted after midnight silently shifts the window by a day, so a policy changed on the business day before can be missed and the file cannot be reproduced later.
quirks.rationale: claimsDailyExtract takes a businessDate job parameter (default: today in pas.extract.business-zone) and selects LAST_UPDATED >= midnight of businessDate - 1 day, the same window start as an on-time nightly run, so a late run or restart can no longer miss the previous business day. Like the JCL there is no upper bound on LAST_UPDATED and the POLICY_STATUS filter is evaluated when the query runs, so a rerun also picks up policies updated after the original run and reflects their current status; a rerun reproduces the original file only if the book has not changed since. Whether to add an upper bound (for example LAST_UPDATED < midnight of businessDate + 1 day) is a contract change for Claims to decide (FU-14).
quirks.parity_note: Identical to the mainframe for runs that start on the business date; ExtractParityIT pins CURRENT DATE to the business date. A late mainframe run is compared with businessDate set to the date it actually ran.

quirks.title: Extract record bytes are not specified anywhere
quirks.description: The JCL only fixes RECFM FB with LRECL 200/150 for the Claims extracts and RECFM FB with LRECL 300 for the exposure CSV, so on the mainframe every EXPOUT record is a fixed 300 bytes, presumably blank padded after the last CSV field. No copybook, header layout or utility control card defines the column positions, number format, NULL representation, CSV header or code page, and DSNTEP2 does not write those DDs at all (Q-30).
quirks.decision_status: proposed - layout is a candidate until production samples (FU-13) and consumer sign-off (FU-14)
quirks.rationale: FeedLayouts holds a candidate: SELECT-list order, text left-aligned and space padded, ISO dates, signed zero-padded decimals with an explicit point, NULL as spaces, fixed-width records padded to the LRECL, CRLF, ISO-8859-1, and an unpadded CSV with a header (the candidate does not pad EXPOUT to 300 bytes). Once the mainframe team supplies a real file, the layout is corrected in one place and must then match byte for byte.
quirks.parity_note: Byte-for-byte comparison against captured mainframe files (tools/extracts/extract_parity.py compare) is blocked on FU-13; until then parity is proven against the JCL SQL rendered with the same layout. The FU-13 samples must show whether EXPOUT lines arrive padded to 300 bytes (RECFM FB) or trimmed by the transfer; if padded, the CSV layout pads too, or Actuarial confirms trimmed lines.

quirks.title: POLNEW accepts a negative policy limit
quirks.description: 3000-VALIDATE-INPUT rejects COVERAGE_LIMIT only when it is EQUAL TO ZERO, although the message reads 'POLICY LIMIT MUST BE GREATER THAN ZERO'. A negative limit entered on POLNMAP passes validation and is stored.
quirks.rationale: The message states the intent. A negative limit is never a valid policy and would reduce the branch accumulation in UNDWRT. The create-policy API rejects a limit <= 0 with the same message.
quirks.parity_note: POLNEW has no parity suite yet; NewBusinessApiIT covers the negative limit.

evidence.contains: POLICY LIMIT MUST BE GREATER THAN ZERO

quirks.title: Holder without credit score: UNDWRT has no null indicator
quirks.description: The policy/holder SELECT in UNDWRT reads CREDIT_SCORE into a host variable without a null indicator. CREDIT_SCORE is nullable, so a holder without a score makes the SELECT fail (SQLCODE -305) and PUWR answers 'POLICY/CUSTOMER DATA NOT FOUND'; the 'no credit score' branch (base 400) is reached only for a stored 0.
quirks.rationale: The COBOL has an explicit branch for a missing score (base 400), which states the intent. The Java underwriter treats a NULL score like 0 and scores the policy instead of reporting it as not found.
quirks.parity_note: Fixtures cannot express NULL host variables; UnderwriterTest covers the NULL score.

quirks.title: POLNEW accepts any policy type and negative amounts
quirks.description: 3000-VALIDATE-INPUT only checks that POLICY-TYPE is not blank and never checks TOTAL_PREMIUM or DEDUCTIBLE. An unknown or lower-case type (e.g. 'XYZ', 'aut') is stored with no default coverages, because 6000-INSERT-COVERAGES matches only AUT/HOM/COM; a negative premium or deductible is stored as entered.
quirks.rationale: Every reader of POLICIES (rating, renewal, underwriting, extracts) assumes one of AUT/HOM/COM/LIF/HLT and non-negative amounts. The create-policy API answers 400 for a type outside that list and for a negative premium or deductible, before any business check.
quirks.parity_note: POLNEW has no parity suite yet; NewBusinessApiIT covers unknown and lower-case types and negative amounts.

quirks.title: Where an underwriting override is stored
quirks.description: UNDWRT writes one UNDERWRITING_DECISIONS row per decision with UNDERWRITER_ID 'SYSTEM' and never sets OVERRIDE_REASON / OVERRIDE_BY, and sets POLICIES.UPDATED_BY to 'UNDWRT'. No program performs overrides today, so their storage is a new decision.
quirks.rationale: The override API updates the latest decision row in place: DECISION_CODE takes the override, OVERRIDE_REASON and OVERRIDE_BY (the caller's own 8-character id from pas_legacy_user, required) are set, UNDERWRITER_ID stays 'SYSTEM' and DECISION_REASON keeps the system text. POLICIES.UW_STATUS follows and POLICIES.UPDATED_BY becomes the overrider. The original system decision code is kept only in the PASAPP.POLICY_AUDIT before-image. Alternative for sign-off: a separate override row, which the DB2 (policy, date) key does not allow on the same day.
quirks.parity_note: No COBOL equivalent; NewBusinessApiIT covers the stored columns and the 403 without a valid pas_legacy_user.

quirks.title: Queue messages are delivered at least once
quirks.description: POLNEW and UNDWRT write the POLICY-RECORD with EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD inside the CICS unit of work, so a committed transaction produces exactly one TD record. The outbox relay, the Kafka bridge and the MQ sink deliver at least once: a crash between publish and acknowledgement repeats a message.
quirks.rationale: Exactly-once across PostgreSQL/DB2, Kafka and MQ would need XA. Every bridged message carries the event id as Kafka header and MQ message property eventId; consumers drop repeats (FileNet by event id, the underwriting queue by event id or policy number + status). Native Kafka consumers use the envelope eventId.
quirks.parity_note: Not a calculation; MessagingBridgeIT asserts one bridged record per event in the normal path.

quirks.title: Bridged POLICY-RECORD reflects the policy at bridge time
quirks.description: The CICS programs write POLICY-RECORD from working storage at the moment of the change. The bridge builds the same 125-byte layout from the current policy row when it consumes the event, so if a second change lands before the first event is bridged both messages carry the later state.
quirks.rationale: Events carry no direct PII (ADR D5) while POLICY-RECORD needs fields the events do not hold, so the record is re-read. Bridge lag is seconds; the same-policy race needs two changes within that window. Consumers that need the exact change state move to the native events, which carry the before/after values.
quirks.parity_note: Byte layout is the AB-519 PolicyRecordCodec (125 bytes, EBCDIC, risk score truncated as in Q-14); MessagingBridgeIT decodes each bridged record.
